prompt: In some families, young children are cared for during the working day by their grandparents. Others believe that professional nurseries provide a better start. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Discussions of this question usually assume a family sitting down to weigh two options. Most are not. Nursery fees in many countries approach a second rent, and the grandparent who takes the child on Tuesday is often the reason one parent can work at all. Any honest answer has to distinguish what would be best for the child from what is actually available to the household.

Taken on its own terms, family care has real advantages that no institution can replicate. A grandparent brings a relationship that predates the arrangement, an attention ratio of one to one, and a tolerance for the slow, repetitive company small children need and paid staff can rarely sustain across a room of twelve. Continuity matters too: the same kitchen, the same walk, the same order to the afternoon. Children under three are steadied by repetition in a way that is easy to dismiss until you watch it removed.

What family care cannot manufacture is other children. Almost everything a four-year-old must learn before school involves negotiating with someone who is not obliged to give way — taking turns, losing an argument, reading a face that has stopped being friendly. Adults who love a child are, quite properly, poor at supplying this, because they concede. Trained staff add a second thing that is easy to overlook: they have seen several hundred children of the same age, so they notice at three what a devoted grandparent may not identify until five.

Weighing the two, I would place a child in a nursery for the year or two before school, precisely because affection is the one thing that can be supplied outside working hours and a peer group is not. But the argument only reaches that conclusion for families who have the choice. For everyone else the useful question is not which setting is superior; it is what a country should do about the cost that decides the matter long before any parent has an opinion.
title: Grandparents or nurseries for young children
